clips.title: The story
paras: Camping 101: Mining is an instructional trade quest directing budding miners to Krunn in Razor Hill. By demonstrating proficiency in their trade, miners learn to forge a Lodestone, a specialized camp fixture that enhances the combat prowess of warriors gathered around a wilderness fire.

Mining offers an honest living that provides practical materials for exploration and survival in the wild. As miners develop their trade and demonstrate proficiency with pick and ore, they can learn to craft specialized campsite equipment. In Durotar, skilled miners are pointed toward Krunn in the settlement of Razor Hill to discover how to forge a Lodestone for their travels.

A Lodestone serves as an attractive centerpiece for adventurers resting in the wilderness. When set up beside a camp, it provides martial fighters gathering by the fire with an added edge to their combat prowess. However, proper camp etiquette requires leaving civilized settlements behind: townsfolk frown upon camps being erected in city squares, meaning travelers must seek the open wild to test their craftsmanship.

Even the sturdiest lodestone is useless without a proper fire to anchor the camp. A basic campfire is necessary before establishing any resting spot, and those unfamiliar with building fires are encouraged to seek out a culinary instructor. Training in the cooking arts ensures that wilderness expeditions have the warmth and basic sustenance required to survive outside town walls.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Mining isn't the most glamorous, but it's good honest work and a fine profession for you to explore.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Lodestone for your camp. Build one of these and everyone who wants to swing a sword will be eager to gather round your fire and soak up the extra "oomph" it can provide to increase their combat prowess.

clips.title: Completion
paras: There you have it, you can now craft your very own Lodestone. Most folk don't care much for camps being set up in the center of town, so you'll need to head into the wilderness if you want to test it out.

Oh, and just remember, no camp is complete without a campfire. You'll need one of those before you start up your camp. Most cooks can teach you to make a fire. If you haven't already, you might want to check in with someone who can train you in the culinary arts to learn the basics.
